claims.text: High-energy ion irradiation of CrMnFeCoNi introduces point defects and defect clusters.
Irradiation-generated point defects and defect clusters act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Defect-induced domain-wall pinning increases the coercive field relative to an unirradiated baseline.
As-cast CrMnFeCoNi is in an equilibrium crystalline state without significant extraneous defect populations.
The proposed intervention is irradiation with 100 MeV Au ions at room temperature, initially near a fluence of 1×10^13 ions/cm².
An irradiation parameter study can identify conditions that maximize domain-wall pinning while preserving magnetic integrity.
There is a defect-density regime that increases domain-wall pinning without causing amorphization or loss of saturation magnetization.
Ion-irradiation defects disrupt the continuity of ferromagnetic exchange paths.
Pinning centers hinder magnetic domain-wall motion.
Hindered domain-wall motion requires a higher applied field to reverse magnetization.
Coercivity will increase measurably and tunably relative to the unirradiated CrMnFeCoNi baseline.
Coercivity enhancement will correlate with engineered defect density up to an optimum.
Beyond the optimal defect density, irradiation damage may degrade other magnetic properties.
Unirradiated CrMnFeCoNi has lower coercivity because it contains fewer domain-wall pinning sites.
The coercivity increase requires retention of the crystalline structure.
Excessive irradiation may cause amorphization, saturation-magnetization degradation, or unwanted phase transformations.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase and the balance between useful pinning and magnetic degradation are uncertain.
